The named-hash declaration cases (sites.go, namedHashes.rv2hv and
chainRv2hv): perl builds rv2hv for a package hash -- an `our`, a `local`, or
no declaration at all -- and padhv for a `my`, a `field`, a signature
parameter or a `state` with its feature on. An element of a package hash
folds into multideref as an element through a reference does, a slice
counts one rv2hv per package hash sliced, and `delete local` keeps the last
level out of multideref. The first rows are hashhedge_test.go's
namedHashTable, each named by its source; the rest are adversarial cases
outside the corpus. Counts are perl 5.44.0's over the whole snippet. The
wider rows are hedges that remain, each with its reason in
hedgereason_test.go: a key that may fold, and a list repeat or a key's own
comma, which perl does not fold.

=== my %h; my @k = keys %h;
my %h; my @k = keys %h;
--- facts
faithful

=== our %h; my @k = keys %h;
our %h; my @k = keys %h;
--- facts
rv2hv 2 exact
faithful

=== local %h; my @k = keys %h;
local %h; my @k = keys %h;
--- facts
rv2hv 2 exact
faithful

=== my @k = keys %h;
my @k = keys %h;
--- facts
rv2hv 1 exact
faithful

=== our (%h, %g);
our (%h, %g);
--- facts
rv2hv 2 exact
faithful

=== local (%h, %g);
local (%h, %g);
--- facts
rv2hv 2 exact
faithful

=== our %h = (a => 1);
our %h = (a => 1);
--- facts
rv2hv 1 exact
faithful

my (%h, %g); my @k = (keys %h, keys %g);

=== inner sub my shadows an our
our %h;
sub f {
  my %h;
  my @k = keys %h;
}
my @k = keys %h;
--- facts
rv2hv 2 exact
faithful

=== local of an our hash under a sub

  local %h;
  my @k = keys %h;
}

rv2hv 3 exact

  my @k = keys %h;
